messages.subject: Passing covdata to fscores()
parts:
Dear Phil,

 

Thank you for taking the team to read this.  I just had a quick question.

 

I am fitting a latent regression model with a b-spline predictor.

 

covdata <- data.frame(decimal = dat$decimal)
mod.all <- mirt(dat.val, model = 1, itemtype = "2PL", technical = list(NCYCLES=5000, theta_lim = c(-6, 6)),
                covdata = covdata, formula = ~ bs(decimal, df = 3))

 

So far, so good.  My issue comes when I try to pass covdat to the fscores function to predict on new data (as suggested in this post: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/mirt-package/covdata$20fscores%7Csort:date/mirt-package/g4ODzpkSl3A/i4fGsQxvAAAJ).  I am trying this code:

 

fscores(mod.all, response.pattern = dat.val[1,], covdata = data.frame(decimal = decimal[1]))

fscores(mod.all, response.pattern = dat.val, covdata = data.frame(decimal = decimal))

 

but getting the:

 

Error in rep(TRUE, nrow(tabdata)) : invalid 'times' argument

 

error message.

 

I am sure I am missing something obvious, but any light you could shed on this would be very much appreciated.

 

Best,

 

Gareth.

Hi,

Thanks for your very quick reply, it is much appricated.

Below is an example on simulated data

Best,

Gareth.

library(mirt)
library(boot)
library(splines)

###############################################################################################################
### Set up a simulation
set.seed(1000)
items <- sort(runif(100, 0, 6))
marg.abils <- sort(rnorm(1000, 0, 0.3))
disc <- rlnorm(100, 0, 0.3)
ages <- sort(runif(1000, 0, 6))
age.adj <- function(age, c=3, t=-0.8) {return(c*(1-exp(age*t)))} # This function gives somethign of a similar shape to my data
plot(ages, age.adj(ages)) # Just checking the function is sensible. it is.

###############################################################################################################
### Simulate some data
sim.resp <- data.frame(matrix(NA, ncol = length(items), nrow = length(abils)))
names(sim.resp) <- 1:length(items)
for(i in 1:length(items)){
  for(j in 1:length(abils)){
    sim.resp[j,i] <- rbinom(1, 1, prob = inv.logit(-disc[i] * (items[i] - (marg.abils[j] + age.adj(ages[j])))))
  }
}

###############################################################################################################
### Ok run the model
covdata <- data.frame(ages = ages)
mod.all <- mirt(sim.resp, model = 1, itemtype = "2PL", technical = list(NCYCLES=5000, theta_lim = c(-6, 6)),
                covdata = covdata, formula = ~ bs(ages, df = 3))
scores <- fscores(mod.all, theta_lim = c(-6, 8)) # It works on the origional data
plot(ages, scores) # Yes, that is what we expect
fscores(mod.all, theta_lim = c(-6, 8), response.pattern = sim.resp, covdata = covdata) # throws the error.
# Error in rep(TRUE, nrow(tabdata)) : invalid 'times' argument

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Passing covdata to fscores()
parts:
I see. Well part of the issue here is that fscores() does not have a covdata input, so whatever is happening is not supporting that input. The other thing though is that the object supplied to fscores() is a single group latent regression model, where internally the covariates and response data are stored separately. Hence, overriding one input requires overriding the other in order to make any sense. 

What you're seeing from the successful fscores() run is the conditional EAP scores, where the latent regression effects are already included for each response pattern. Supplying different response patterns and covdata inputs is a bit more awkward because you technically need to create a new fitted model object with the associated response patterns and data, where the IRT parameter estimates are fixed at the previously estimated values from the first model (clunky, I know, but that's the best option for now). I could add support for the response.pattern + covdata inputs at a later time though, which would save this two-step approach. But for now it doesn't seem that essential given the workaround. HTH.

Phil
